objective: Test whether UberBond can synthesize a behaviorally missing reusable representation primitive from a target-blind integer-structure state-machine grammar, freeze it, and transfer it to distinct tasks.

hiddenTarget.description: Parity of the total number of prime factors with multiplicity.

structuralProgramGrammar.concept: Generic divisor-sweep state machines over a mutable working integer.
structuralProgramGrammar.selector: Discovery train accuracy, then discovery validation accuracy, then lower program-description cost, then lexical program ID.
structuralProgramGrammar.restriction: The grammar exposes only generic loops, divisibility tests, division, one-bit state updates, and leftover handling. It contains no target-named arithmetic primitive.

split.hash: 32-bit deterministic mix: +0x9e3779b9; xor>>16; *0x85ebca6b; xor>>13; *0xc2b2ae35; xor>>16; unsigned; mod 5
split.law: Discovery primitive selection may use only training and validation labels. The primitive is frozen before discovery-held-out and all transfer scoring.

falsifier: Selected program violates the target-blind grammar or embeds a forbidden target primitive.
Fewer than two transfer tasks pass both transfer thresholds.
Held-out or transfer labels influence primitive synthesis.
Search candidate count, selected description cost, or baseline burden is omitted.
Semantic novelty admission is invalidated by an exact base-ontology equivalent.
promotionBoundary: A pass supports only a deterministic finite synthetic claim that a target-blind structural grammar synthesized and reused a behaviorally missing primitive. It does not establish open-ended ontology invention, autonomous mathematics, scientific discovery, physical discovery, or general intelligence.
